# tinyvec - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tinyvec/^1/

## Expand description

`tinyvec` provides 100% safe vec-like data structures.

[§](https://docs.rs#provided-types)Provided Types

With no features enabled, this crate provides the [ ArrayVec](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayVec.html) type, which
is an array-backed storage. You can push values into the array and pop them
out of the array and so on. If the array is made to overflow it will panic.

Similarly, there is also a [ SliceVec](https://docs.rs/struct.SliceVec.html) type available, which is a vec-like
that’s backed by a slice you provide. You can add and remove elements, but
if you overflow the slice it will panic.

With the `alloc` feature enabled, the crate also has a [ TinyVec](https://docs.rs/enum.TinyVec.html) type.
This is an enum type which is either an

`Inline(ArrayVec)` or a `Heap(Vec)`.
If a `TinyVec` is `Inline` and would overflow it automatically transitions
itself into being `Heap` mode instead of a panic.All of this is done with no `unsafe` code within the crate. Technically the
`Vec` type from the standard library uses `unsafe` internally, but *this
crate* introduces no new `unsafe` code into your project.

The limitation is that the element type of a vec from this crate must
support the [ Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) trait. This means that this crate isn’t suitable for
all situations, but a very surprising number of types do support

`Default`.[§](https://docs.rs#other-features)Other Features

- `grab_spare_slice`lets you get access to the “inactive” portions of an ArrayVec.
- `serde`provides a- `Serialize`and- `Deserialize`implementation for- `TinyVec`- `ArrayVec`
- `borsh`provides a- `BorshSerialize`and- `BorshDeserialize`implementation for- `TinyVec`- `ArrayVec`
- `defmt`provides a- `Format`implementation for all types, provided the inner item also has an implementation.

[§](https://docs.rs#api)API

The general goal of the crate is that, as much as possible, the vecs here
should be a “drop in” replacement for the standard library `Vec` type. We
strive to provide all of the `Vec` methods with the same names and
signatures. The exception is that the element type of some methods will have
a `Default` bound that’s not part of the normal `Vec` type.

The vecs here also have a few additional methods that aren’t on the `Vec`
type. In this case, the names tend to be fairly long so that they are
unlikely to clash with any future methods added to `Vec`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayVec.html)- Vec
- An array-backed, vector-like data structure.
- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayVecDrain.html)- VecDrain
- Draining iterator for `ArrayVec`
- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayVecIterator.html)- VecIterator
- Iterator for consuming an `ArrayVec`and returning owned elements.
- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayVecSplice.html)- VecSplice
- Splicing iterator for `ArrayVec`See`ArrayVec::splice`
- [Slice](https://docs.rs/struct.SliceVec.html)- Vec
- A slice-backed vector-like data structure.
- [Slice](https://docs.rs/struct.SliceVecDrain.html)- VecDrain
- Draining iterator for `SliceVec`
- [Tiny](https://docs.rs/struct.TinyVecSplice.html)- VecSplice - `alloc`
- Splicing iterator for `TinyVec`See`TinyVec::splice`
- [TryFrom](https://docs.rs/struct.TryFromSliceError.html)- Slice - Error
- The error type returned when a conversion from a slice to an `ArrayVec`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- A vector that starts inline, but can automatically move to the heap.
- [Tiny](https://docs.rs/enum.TinyVecDrain.html)- VecDrain - `alloc`
- Draining iterator for `TinyVecDrain`

# unicode_normalization - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unicode-normalization/0.1.25/target-redirect/unicode_normalization/

## Expand description

Unicode character composition and decomposition utilities
as described in
[Unicode Standard Annex #15](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/).

```
extern crate unicode_normalization;
use unicode_normalization::char::compose;
use unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization;
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(compose('A','\u{30a}'), Some('Å'));
    let s = "ÅΩ";
    let c = s.nfc().collect::<String>();
    assert_eq!(c, "ÅΩ");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#cratesio)crates.io

You can use this package in your project by adding the following
to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
unicode-normalization = "0.1.20"
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [char](https://docs.rs/char/index.html)
- Methods for composing and decomposing characters.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Decompositions](https://docs.rs/struct.Decompositions.html)
- External iterator for a string decomposition’s characters.
- [Recompositions](https://docs.rs/struct.Recompositions.html)
- External iterator for a string recomposition’s characters.
- [Replacements](https://docs.rs/struct.Replacements.html)
- External iterator for replacements for a string’s characters.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamSafe.html)- Safe
- [UAX15-D4](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/#UAX15-D4): This iterator keeps track of how many non-starters there have been since the last starter in- *NFKD*and will emit a Combining Grapheme Joiner (U+034F) if the count exceeds 30.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [IsNormalized](https://docs.rs/enum.IsNormalized.html)
- QuickCheck quickly determines if a string is normalized, it can return
`Maybe`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [Unicode](https://docs.rs/trait.UnicodeNormalization.html)- Normalization
- Methods for iterating over strings while applying Unicode normalizations
as described in
[Unicode Standard Annex #15](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_nfc](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfc.html)
- Authoritatively check if a string is in NFC.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfc_quick.html)- nfc_ - quick
- Quickly check if a string is in NFC, potentially returning
`IsNormalized::Maybe`if further checks are necessary. In this case a check like`s.chars().nfc().eq(s.chars())`should suffice.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfc_stream_safe.html)- nfc_ - stream_ - safe
- Authoritatively check if a string is Stream-Safe NFC.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfc_stream_safe_quick.html)- nfc_ - stream_ - safe_ - quick
- Quickly check if a string is Stream-Safe NFC.
- [is_nfd](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfd.html)
- Authoritatively check if a string is in NFD.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfd_quick.html)- nfd_ - quick
- Quickly check if a string is in NFD.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfd_stream_safe.html)- nfd_ - stream_ - safe
- Authoritatively check if a string is Stream-Safe NFD.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfd_stream_safe_quick.html)- nfd_ - stream_ - safe_ - quick
- Quickly check if a string is Stream-Safe NFD.
- [is_nfkc](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfkc.html)
- Authoritatively check if a string is in NFKC.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfkc_quick.html)- nfkc_ - quick
- Quickly check if a string is in NFKC.
- [is_nfkd](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfkd.html)
- Authoritatively check if a string is in NFKD.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_nfkd_quick.html)- nfkd_ - quick
- Quickly check if a string is in NFKD.

# IsNormalized in unicode_normalization - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-normalization/^0.1.12/enum.IsNormalized.html

```
pub enum IsNormalized {
    Yes,
    No,
    Maybe,
}
```
## Expand description

QuickCheck quickly determines if a string is normalized, it can return
`Maybe`

The QuickCheck algorithm can quickly determine if a text is or isn’t
normalized without any allocations in many cases, but it has to be able to
return `Maybe` when a full decomposition and recomposition is necessary.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Yes)

### Yes

The text is definitely normalized.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.No)

### No

The text is definitely not normalized.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Maybe)

### Maybe

The text may be normalized.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_normalization/lib.rs.html#129)

#### fn [cjk_compat_variants](https://docs.rs#tymethod.cjk_compat_variants)(self) -> [Replacements](https://docs.rs/struct.Replacements.html)<I> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

A transformation which replaces [CJK Compatibility Ideograph](https://www.unicode.org/glossary/#compatibility_ideograph) codepoints
with normal forms using [Standardized Variation Sequences](https://www.unicode.org/glossary/#standardized_variation_sequence). This is not
part of the canonical or compatibility decomposition algorithms, but
performing it before those algorithms produces normalized output which
better preserves the intent of the original text.

Note that many systems today ignore variation selectors, so these may not immediately help text display as intended, but they at least preserve the information in a standardized form, giving implementations the option to recognize them.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# is_nfc_quick in unicode_normalization - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-normalization/^0.1.12/fn.is_nfc_quick.html

`pub fn is_nfc_quick<I: `[Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = [char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html)>>(s: I) -> [IsNormalized](https://docs.rs/enum.IsNormalized.html)## Expand description

Quickly check if a string is in NFC, potentially returning
`IsNormalized::Maybe` if further checks are necessary.  In this case a check
like `s.chars().nfc().eq(s.chars())` should suffice.

# ScriptExtension in unicode_script - Rust

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_script/lib.rs.html#236-238)#### pub fn [intersect_with](https://docs.rs#method.intersect_with)(&mut self, other: Self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_script/lib.rs.html#236-238)

#### pub fn [intersect_with](https://docs.rs#method.intersect_with)(&mut self, other: Self)

Intersect this `ScriptExtension` with another `ScriptExtension`. Produces `Unknown` if things
do not intersect. This is equivalent to [ ScriptExtension::intersection](https://docs.rs/struct.ScriptExtension.html#method.intersection) but it stores the result
in

`self`“Common” (`Zyyy`) and “Inherited” (`Zinh`) are considered as intersecting
everything, the intersection of `Common` and `Inherited` is `Inherited`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_script/lib.rs.html#245-256)#### pub const fn [intersection](https://docs.rs#method.intersection)(self, other: Self) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_script/lib.rs.html#245-256)

#### pub const fn [intersection](https://docs.rs#method.intersection)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Find the intersection between two ScriptExtensions. Returns Unknown if things do not intersect.

“Common” (`Zyyy`) and “Inherited” (`Zinh`) are considered as intersecting
everything, the intersection of `Common` and `Inherited` is `Inherited`

Find the union between two ScriptExtensions.

“Common” (`Zyyy`) and “Inherited” (`Zinh`) are considered as intersecting
everything, the union of `Common` and `Inherited` is `Common`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_script/lib.rs.html#280-282)#### pub fn [contains_script](https://docs.rs#method.contains_script)(self, script: [Script](https://docs.rs/enum.Script.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/unicode_script/lib.rs.html#280-282)

#### pub fn [contains_script](https://docs.rs#method.contains_script)(self, script: [Script](https://docs.rs/enum.Script.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)

Check if this ScriptExtension contains the given script

Should be used with specific scripts only, this will
return `true` if `self` is not `Unknown` and `script` is
`Common` or `Inherited`

# unicode_security - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unicode-security/latest/target-redirect/unicode_security/index.html

## Expand description

Detect possible security problems with Unicode usage according to
[Unicode Technical Standard #39](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/)
rules.

```
extern crate unicode_security;
use unicode_security::GeneralSecurityProfile;
fn main() {
    let ch = 'µ'; // U+00B5 MICRO SIGN
    let allowed = 'µ'.identifier_allowed();
    println!("{}", ch);
    println!("The above char is {} in unicode identifiers.",
             if allowed { "allowed" } else { "restricted" });
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)features

unicode-security supports a `no_std` feature. This eliminates dependence
on std, and instead uses equivalent functions from core.

[§](https://docs.rs#cratesio)crates.io

You can use this package in your project by adding the following
to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
unicode-security = "0.0.1"
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use confusable_detection::`- [skeleton](https://docs.rs/confusable_detection/fn.skeleton.html);
- `pub use general_security_profile::`- [GeneralSecurityProfile](https://docs.rs/general_security_profile/trait.GeneralSecurityProfile.html);
- `pub use mixed_script::`- [is_potential_mixed_script_confusable_char](https://docs.rs/mixed_script/fn.is_potential_mixed_script_confusable_char.html);
- `pub use mixed_script::`- [MixedScript](https://docs.rs/mixed_script/trait.MixedScript.html);
- `pub use restriction_level::`- [RestrictionLevel](https://docs.rs/restriction_level/enum.RestrictionLevel.html);
- `pub use restriction_level::`- [RestrictionLevelDetection](https://docs.rs/restriction_level/trait.RestrictionLevelDetection.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [confusable_](https://docs.rs/confusable_detection/index.html)- detection
- [Confusable detection](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#Confusable_Detection)
- [general_](https://docs.rs/general_security_profile/index.html)- security_ - profile
- Utilities for working with the [General Security Profile](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#General_Security_Profile)for identifiers
- [mixed_](https://docs.rs/mixed_script/index.html)- script
- [Mixed-script detection](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#Mixed_Script_Detection)
- [restriction_](https://docs.rs/restriction_level/index.html)- level
- For detecting the [restriction level](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/#Restriction_Level_Detection)a string conforms to

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! [Unicode Technical Standard #39](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr39/)

[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! use unicode_security::GeneralSecurityProfile;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! fn main() {
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!     let ch = 'µ'; // U+00B5 MICRO SIGN
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!     let allowed = 'µ'.identifier_allowed();
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!     println!("{}", ch);
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!     println!("The above char is {} in unicode identifiers.",
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!              if allowed { "allowed" } else { "restricted" });
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! }
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ```
